title: Soft-deadline adaptive batcher — trace & tuning notes
content:
Background:
We continue to see hard-to-predict tail latency in low to medium QPS tiers when using continuous batching. Existing heuristics (age-weighted, size-first) help throughput but allow 'deadline slippage' for a subset of requests that wait multiple timeouts before being scheduled. This doc captures an exploration of a soft-deadline adaptive batcher: a scheduler that enforces an increasing priority for requests as they age and opens a short "grace window" to allow near-deadline coalescing while bounding the worst-case wait.

Goals:
- Reduce p99/p99.9 latency without regressing throughput more than 5% for medium bursty workloads.
- Keep p50/p90 stable.
- Produce reproducible traces and a clear experiment matrix for CI and manual runs.

Hypotheses:
1) A soft-deadline policy (per-request deadlines that escalate priority) will lower tail latency by ensuring requests that would otherwise be preempted get served earlier.
2) Introducing a small grace window (e.g., 1-3ms extra wait for batch completion) will allow better packing without meaningful tail regressions if combined with dynamic priority escalation.
3) The biggest bottleneck shift will be in the batching decision hot path (lock contention + kernel selection), so tracing both CPU and NVTX/GPU timelines is required.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Workloads:
  * Steady 50rps (long-tail token lengths: 16, 128)
  * Bursty synthetic: Poisson spikes to 300rps for 200ms every 2s
  * Real traffic replay (extracted sample from prod replay job replay/2024-11-01)
- Policy knobs:
  * baseline: size-first, timeout=8ms
  * soft-deadline-1: deadline-scale=linear, base-timeout=6ms, grace=2ms
  * soft-deadline-2: deadline-scale=exp, base-timeout=4ms, grace=1ms
  * priority-cap: max-priority-age=40ms
- Observed metrics:
  * p50/p90/p99/p99.9 end-to-end latency (ms)
  * scheduler enqueue/wait/hold times (ms)
  * batches-per-second and avg batch size (tokens / requests)
  * throughput (tokens/sec)
  * GPU occupancy and kernel time (ms)
  * CPU scheduling stalls and lock contention profile

Instrumentation plan:
- Distributed trace: attach trace_id at request ingress, propagate to runtime and CUDA NVTX marks for kernel boundaries. Use our existing tracer (tracer-service: v0.9.4) to link to logs.
- Kernel-level: NVTX ranges around batch formation and kernel launch.
- CPU: perf + flamegraphs on the scheduler thread; collect with 'perf record -F 99 -g --pid <serve_pid>' during run.
- eBPF: capture sys_enter/sys_exit and context-switch counts for the worker processes to detect preemption.
- Prom queries to collect metrics during a run: 
  * rate(redwood_batcher_batches_created_total[1m])
  * histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  * avg_over_time(redwood_scheduler_queue_depth[1m])
- Trace sampling rule: sample 100% for synthetic runs, 5-10% for replay runs. Attach local trace viewer link in run notes.

Runbook (single experiment):
1) Start metrics/trace collector: ./scripts/start-collectors.sh --out runs/soft-deadline-<tag>
2) Deploy batcher build: git checkout pr/678; bazel run //cmd/serve -- --batcher-config=soft-deadline-1
3) Start workload generator: ./bench/gen_poisson --qps 300 --burst 200ms --pattern conf/replay-sample.json --out run.json
4) After 10 minutes, stop workload; upload traces: ./scripts/collect-artifacts.sh runs/soft-deadline-<tag>
5) Run analysis notebook: notebooks/compare-soft-deadline.ipynb (bind to collected prometheus snapshot)

Preliminary observations (from two quick local runs):
- soft-deadline-1 reduced p99 by ~18% on the Poisson-burst workload vs baseline, while throughput dropped ~3%.
- p99.9 improvement is larger (~28%) but only in runs where bursts align with batching timeouts (expected).
- We saw an unexpected increase in scheduler lock contention (measured via perf) when grace window > 2ms; suspect additional bookkeeping per-request priority update is contended.
- GPU kernel time per-batch decreased slightly (better packing), but GPU idle spikes appeared when the scheduler delayed launching small batches to wait for grace, causing occasional sub-ms underutilization.

Instrument findings (notes):
- NVTX traces clearly show kernel launch bursts separated by scheduler decision stalls (~0.5-1.5ms).
- Flamegraphs show majority of time in batcher->attempt_coalesce() and ordering heap adjustments; profiling indicates we can micro-opt: use a lock-free age-bucket queue for the hot path.
- eBPF shows context switches increase by ~12% under soft-deadline-1, correlating with additional timer wakeups.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Risk: grace window can hide pathological traffic patterns that force repeated reordering and starvation of very short requests. Mitigation: add max-deadline-cap and an anti-starvation fast-path that forces immediate flush if request age > threshold.
- Risk: added per-request metadata increases memory churn. Mitigation: pool objects and avoid heap allocations on the hot path.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Implement age-bucket queue prototype (Ravi) and bench vs current heap-based priority queue. (owner: Ravi, ETA: 2025-01-12)
- Add lock striping to scheduler state to reduce contention. (owner: Aisha, ETA: 2025-01-20)
- Run full replay tests against prod-sampled traffic for 24h and collect p99.9 heatmap. (owner: Michael, ETA: 2025-01-30)
- Add CI microbenchmark that simulates Poisson bursts and checks p99 under 20ms for medium machines. (owner: infra-qe, ticket: JIRA:INF-5010)

Open questions for the group:
- What are acceptable throughput regressions for Dedicated customers on the mid-tier (SLA vs economics)? Product input needed.
- Should grace windows be adaptive (learned from recent inter-arrival stats) or static per-deployment tier?
- Is NVTX instrumentation at this granularity acceptable for production builds, or do we gate it behind flags only enabled in debug/benchmark runs?

Notes-to-self: 
- Capture a short demo GIF of the trace viewer showing before/after NVTX timelines for the PR. Good for sync deck.
- Document the anti-starvation fast-path clearly in the rollout playbook (console/rollouts/docs).

References: 
- Related tickets: JIRA:INF-4728 (batching heuristics retrospective), JIRA:INF-4921 (current feature PR)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/678
- Slack thread: #eng-runtime: p12345 (linked above)

Raw commands used in quick runs: 
- perf record: perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pidof redwood-serv) -- sleep 60
- NVTX profiling: export REDWOOD_NVTX=1 && ./bazel-bin/cmd/serve --batcher-config=soft-deadline-1
- run generator: ./bench/gen_poisson --qps 50 --pattern conf/len16.json --duration 600

If you review this, add comments inline or drop notes in the slack thread. Will convert to a more formal playbook if the age-bucket prototype looks promising.

-- Michael
